jsonld.name: 529 College Savings Calculator
jsonld.description: Calculate how much your 529 college savings plan will grow. Enter starting balance, monthly contributions, return rate, and years to see projected college fund value.

acceptedAnswer.text: In the US, 529 plan growth is generally tax-free when used for qualified education expenses, though specific rules and any state tax benefits vary — check your specific plan and jurisdiction's rules for details.

mainEntity.name: What if I don't know exactly how much college will cost yet?

acceptedAnswer.text: That's normal this far in advance — many families use a general savings target and adjust contributions over time as costs and the child's education path become clearer, rather than trying to pinpoint an exact number today.

mainEntity.name: How much will my 529 grow in 10 years?

acceptedAnswer.text: A 529 plan with $10,000 starting balance and $250/month contributions at 6% annual return grows to approximately $59,000 after 10 years. Use this calculator to project your specific 529 growth.

mainEntity.name: What is the average 529 plan growth rate?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most 529 plan age-based portfolios target 5-7% annual growth for long investment horizons, shifting to more conservative allocations (2-4%) as college approaches. Use your fund's historical return as your estimate.

mainEntity.name: How much should I have in a 529 by age 10?

acceptedAnswer.text: A common benchmark is saving roughly one-third of expected college costs by the time the child is 10. For a $60,000 target, that's around $20,000 by age 10. This calculator helps you see if your current savings pace will hit your goal.

mainEntity.name: How much should I have saved in a 529 plan by age?

acceptedAnswer.text: A common benchmark: save roughly 1/3 of expected 4-year college costs by age 10, 2/3 by age 15, and 100% by the time the child starts college. For a $80,000 4-year college goal: $27,000 by age 10, $53,000 by age 15. Use this calculator to find your required monthly savings.

mainEntity.name: What is the average 529 plan return rate?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most age-based 529 portfolios target 5-8% annual returns for children 10+ years from college, gradually shifting to more conservative investments (2-4%) as college approaches. Historical average for a diversified stock fund is approximately 7% annually, though past performance does not guarantee future results.

mainEntity.name: How do I choose between a 529 plan calculator for different states?

acceptedAnswer.text: You are not required to use your home state's 529 plan. Compare your state's plan (which may offer a state tax deduction) with other states' plans on fees and investment options. Use this calculator to compare projected growth across different contribution levels and return rates.

mainEntity.name: What is a 529 college savings plan?

acceptedAnswer.text: A 529 plan is a tax-advantaged savings account specifically for education expenses. Contributions grow tax-free, and withdrawals for qualified education expenses (tuition, books, room and board) are also tax-free. Most US states offer their own 529 plan, but you can use any state's plan regardless of where you live or where your child attends college.

mainEntity.name: How much should I save per month in a 529 plan?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on your target and timeline. If you expect college to cost $60,000 and have 10 years to save at a 6% return, saving the full amount takes about $366/month, while covering one-third ($20,000) takes about $122/month. Use this calculator to model your specific situation based on your child's age and your target college fund amount.

mainEntity.name: What is the average return on a 529 plan?

acceptedAnswer.text: 529 plans invested in age-based portfolios (which automatically shift from stocks to bonds as college approaches) have historically returned 5-7% annually when the child is young, declining to 2-4% as college nears. A conservative planning estimate is 5-6% average annual return over a long horizon.

mainEntity.name: Can I use a 529 for K-12 private school?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. In 2026, up to $20,000 a year per beneficiary can be withdrawn tax-free for K-12 tuition (the limit was $10,000). Check whether your state treats these withdrawals the same way.

You can change the beneficiary to another family member, keep it for graduate school, or roll up to $35,000 over a lifetime into the beneficiary's Roth IRA if the account has been open 15 years. Non-qualified withdrawals pay income tax and a 10% additional tax on the earnings.

mainEntity.name: How much can I put into a 529 at once?

acceptedAnswer.text: A single giver can contribute up to $95,000 per child in 2026 by electing five years of the $19,000 gift tax exclusion at once ($190,000 for a married couple). Plan balance limits are set by each state.

mainEntity.name: How much do I need to save each month if I start when my child is 10?

acceptedAnswer.text: To fully fund four years at an in-state public college with costs rising 4% a year and a 6% return, about $1,880 a month from a $0 balance. Starting at birth takes about $596. Most families set a lower coverage target.

mainEntity.name: How much will college cost when my newborn enrolls?

acceptedAnswer.text: At 5% yearly cost growth, four years at an in-state public college that costs $114,000 today would be about $274,355. At 3% it would be about $194,077.
